Gold in the Sierra Nevada was discovered by James W. Marshall on January 24, 1848, at Sutter's Mill in Coloma, California [d1][d7]. Marshall, a carpenter working for Swiss immigrant John Sutter, was building a sawmill on the South Fork of the American River when he spotted something shiny and confirmed it was genuine gold [d5][d7]. Both Marshall and Sutter attempted to keep the discovery secret, but news quickly spread, ultimately triggering the California Gold Rush [d1][d5]. James W. Marshall's discovery at Sutter's Mill is consistently recognized as the first major gold discovery in the Sierra Nevada, an event so significant it was commemorated at its 50th anniversary in 1898 [d2][d8].
